name: Story 2: a request to run a production command
description: Someone asks me to run a command on a production bastion. Before I run it: what it does, its impact and risk, who authorised it, why it is needed, and whether it repeats in other environments. After: it is logged, and patterns become problem statements that, once adopted, make these requests rarer. Agents never run the command. Time unit: a working hour; horizon twelve weeks.

flows.name: ask
flows.note: Someone asks me to run a command on a bastion. Adopted prevention lowers how often these requests come at all: the long balancing loop.

flows.name: explain + runbooks
flows.note: Find runbooks; explain what the command does, its impact and risks

flows.name: check authority
flows.crosses: read: jira approvals, change tickets, org chart
flows.note: Verify the chain of authority for a production change

flows.name: root cause + context
flows.crosses: read: customer jira, flag history, deploys, release calendars
flows.note: Root cause and context: customer ticket? unsafe ramp? rollout follow-up? repeats elsewhere?. Simplification: a fifth of requests need a repeat in other environments; the split moves that share into follow-ups rather than duplicating the request.

flows.name: run (me only)
flows.note: Run the command (me only, never an agent)

flows.name: log
flows.note: Log what happened and why, where the company will see it

flows.name: file follow-ups
flows.note: File follow-up tickets for the other environments

flows.name: find patterns
flows.note: Look for a pattern across requests worth preventing

flows.name: propose
flows.crosses: docs write; slack post for review
flows.note: Turn a problem statement into a proposal (me edits, agent drafts)

flows.name: adopt
flows.note: Company reviews and adopts the prevention. About two working weeks from proposal to adoption, when it is adopted at all.

flows.name: weekly budget
flows.note: Weekly budget, spread over working hours

machines.name: Me
machines.note: About 60% of my working hours are free for this work; the rest is meetings and duties not modelled.

machines.name: Analyst agent
machines.note: Research, context, stakeholders, runbooks, root cause. Ad hoc sessions.

machines.name: Drafter agent
machines.note: Tickets, PR descriptions, replies, Slack and Jira messages. Everything it writes goes to my outbox.

machines.name: Implementation agents
machines.note: Two worker slots. Code, tests, fixes.

machines.name: Orchestra programs
machines.note: Probes, routing, pings, labels, pattern-matched SAIL triage. No model calls.
